domain_grades.name: developer-automation-and-fixtures
notes: Automation scripts have meaningful validation and fixture-based checks in place.
Quality is good where tests exist, with clear expected outcomes and deterministic script behavior.
Coverage is thinner than runtime/testing domains, especially for malformed and drift scenarios.
Conventions are mostly followed but would benefit from stronger static shell analysis and clearer fixture documentation.

dimension_rationale.convention_adherence: Automation conventions are reasonably consistent and integrated with repository validation. Lack of shell static-analysis gates and fixture intent docs keeps adherence from being higher.
dimension_rationale.risk_exposure: Risk is moderate because script and fixture drift can silently erode validation reliability. These paths are smaller than runtime code but still impact agent feedback loops.
dimension_rationale.test_coverage: This domain has targeted checks but lower breadth than runtime Rust code. Script/fixture variants are not comprehensively exercised across failure shapes.
dimension_rationale.test_quality: Existing tests appear behavior-aware and practical for automation workflows. The remaining gap is depth and range, not basic assertion correctness.

domain_grades.name: integration-and-contract-testing
notes: The integration and contract suite is broad, including phase, lint, CLI, and contract checks.
Assertion quality is strong and generally validates real behavior rather than smoke-only outcomes.
End-to-end breadth is still limited, with too few multi-worker/full-runtime scenario paths.
Conventions are well represented in tests, but maintenance efficiency is impacted by some repetitive and ignored patterns.

dimension_rationale.convention_adherence: Conventions are encoded in many contract tests and validation checks. The score is slightly reduced by gaps in tooling consistency and test-surface maintainability.
dimension_rationale.risk_exposure: This domain lowers overall risk by exercising many cross-component flows. Risk is still moderate because orchestration boundary modules are not uniformly covered.
dimension_rationale.test_coverage: Coverage is strong in this domain due to many integration and contract tests touching runtime behavior. Confidence is reduced by limited explicit e2e scenario diversity.
dimension_rationale.test_quality: Tests are generally deterministic and behavior-rich, with clear failure signal. Remaining weaknesses are structural (coverage distribution and deeper invariant checks), not basic assertion hygiene.

domain_grades.name: runtime-orchestration
notes: Unit-test presence is strong across core Rust runtime modules and key orchestration paths.
Test assertions are behavior-focused and cover edge cases in parser, state, and TUI flows.
Risk remains elevated because high-complexity logic is concentrated in a few large files and several boundary modules are untested.
Conventions are mostly followed, but policy/tooling inconsistencies (for example clippy flag drift) reduce confidence.

dimension_rationale.convention_adherence: Runtime conventions are well established and often mechanically enforced through lint/test policy. Remaining inconsistencies in enforcement workflows keep the score below top-tier.
dimension_rationale.risk_exposure: This area carries the largest operational risk due to large coupled files and untested runtime entry/boundary modules. These paths are sensitive to regressions that can pass local checks but fail in orchestration.
dimension_rationale.test_coverage: Coverage is high because runtime modules and phase behavior are tested broadly in Rust. The main miss is thinner full-runtime e2e protection on orchestration boundaries.
dimension_rationale.test_quality: Test quality is excellent with specific names and meaningful assertions across state transitions and parsing. The score is not perfect because some validation relies on weaker substring checks and lacks property/fuzz depth.

deficiencies.description: Critical runtime boundary modules such as `config.rs`, `phase_cli.rs`, `plan_phase.rs`, `merge_loop.rs`, `pr_audit.rs`, and `main.rs` lack sufficient tests. Without coverage at these entrypoints, agents cannot reliably validate that orchestration edits preserve startup, planning, merge, and CLI invariants.
deficiencies.suggested_task_title: Cover Runtime Boundary Modules With Contracts
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add focused contract/integration tests per boundary module using existing phase fixture patterns. Assert success and failure paths for startup, config resolution, planning, merge loop decisions, and CLI invocation behavior.

deficiencies.description: A very large in-file test module in `tui.rs` mixes rendering, parser, and input concerns. This degrades agent productivity because unrelated failures collide in one dense surface, making localization and safe edits slower.
deficiencies.suggested_task_title: Split TUI Test Modules By Concern
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Refactor the current in-file tests into focused files such as rendering, parsing, and input behavior modules. Keep shared builders/helpers in a common test utility module to preserve coverage while improving triage speed.

deficiencies.description: Clippy policy is internally inconsistent: workspace denies `expect_used` while validation script allows it. Agents can pass one enforcement path and fail another, creating avoidable churn.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Remove the `-A clippy::expect_used` override from validation scripts or scope/document it intentionally to non-production targets. Keep one canonical policy enforced identically across local and CI paths.

deficiencies.description: End-to-end scenario breadth is too narrow, with only a single explicit e2e file covering full runtime behavior. Without broader multi-worker and failure-recovery e2e paths, autonomous agents can pass integration suites while missing cross-phase regressions that appear only in full orchestration runs.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add 3-5 additional e2e tests that execute the `gardener` binary through multi-worker sync, quit-after, and recovery flows. Reuse existing fixtures and assert lifecycle outcomes, exit status, and expected log markers.

deficiencies.description: Steering guidance covers runtime invocation but not domain-level verification workflows for tests and scripts. Agents must infer what to run, which increases skipped checks and inconsistent validation before changes are proposed.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Extend `AGENTS.md` with concise sections for runtime, integration/contract tests, and script/fixture validation. Include exact commands and expected outcomes for each domain.

deficiencies.description: Coverage gating excludes files through an ignore manifest, reducing denominator trust. Agents may modify excluded high-risk code and still satisfy coverage thresholds, masking real regression risk.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Review `scripts/coverage-ignore-manifest.txt`, remove non-essential exclusions, and require justification comments for remaining entries. Add policy checks that block new ignores without explicit approval.

deficiencies.description: Coverage denominator narrowing via ignore manifest can overstate runtime confidence. Agents may treat green thresholds as strong evidence even when critical paths are excluded from measurement.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Require explicit rationale and review for each ignored runtime path and remove stale exclusions. Add a policy test that blocks broad or high-risk new ignore entries.

deficiencies.description: Automation script and fixture validation is uneven, especially around malformed and drifted cases. This weakens agent trust in local checks, because scripts may report green for nominal inputs while failing in real-world degraded states.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Create table-driven integration tests for valid, malformed, and drifted fixture states under `scripts/fixtures/check-migrations-wired/`. Assert strict outputs and exit codes so failures are deterministic and actionable.

deficiencies.description: Very large monolithic files in runtime logic increase coupling and retest surface for small changes. Agents must load and reason about too much context, raising accidental regression probability and slowing iteration.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Split large files by responsibility (rendering/input/state mapping/parsing or lifecycle partitions). Keep tests co-located with new modules to preserve behavior signal while reducing blast radius.

deficiencies.description: Pre-commit currently runs a heavy full validation path including full-target coverage on every commit. Agents making small edits pay long feedback latency, reducing iteration throughput and increasing context switching.
deficiencies.suggested_task_title: Split Fast And Full Validation Tiers
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Create `validate-fast` and `validate-full` targets, with fast checks in pre-commit and full checks required in CI. Ensure fast tier still catches common local regressions quickly.

deficiencies.description: Core public runtime APIs have sparse rustdoc coverage, especially in central modules. Agents must infer contracts from implementation details, increasing misunderstanding risk in startup/config/worker flows.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add module-level `//!` docs and targeted `///` contracts for key public types/functions in config, startup, worker pool, and library boundaries. Focus on lifecycle guarantees, failure modes, and ownership expectations.

deficiencies.description: There is no explicit build/test command matrix for common scopes. This forces agents to spend turns discovering commands and can lead to under-testing or unnecessarily expensive full-suite runs.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add a compact command table for build, unit, integration, lint, and coverage at both package and workspace scope. Include fast-path commands for changed areas and full-path commands for pre-merge verification.

deficiencies.description: No dependency/security scan gate is visible in validation or CI workflows. Agents can update dependencies and still get green checks while introducing known vulnerabilities or policy violations.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Integrate `cargo audit` and/or `cargo deny check` into CI with fail-on-findings policy. Add a local invocation path so agents can run the same checks before commit.

deficiencies.description: There is no hard CI policy preventing growth of untested source inventory in high-risk paths. Agents can land new uncovered runtime code while still passing aggregate checks, allowing risk to accumulate silently.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Introduce a CI check that fails when new untested files appear under runtime orchestration paths. Ratchet allowed counts downward over time with explicit exception workflow.

deficiencies.description: Script and fixture layers lack dedicated coverage tooling and thresholds. Agents depend on these automation paths for validation, so blind spots here can hide branch/path regressions.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Introduce script coverage tooling (for example, `kcov`) for high-impact scripts and wire thresholds into CI. Prioritize fixture-sensitive scripts first, then expand incrementally.

deficiencies.description: Validation does not enforce rustdoc generation or staged missing-docs policy. Documentation regressions can merge silently, reducing API discoverability and forcing agents into costly code spelunking.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Include `cargo doc --no-deps` in validation and introduce staged `missing_docs` enforcement for high-centrality modules. Start as warnings and ratchet to stricter policy once baseline improves.

deficiencies.description: Worktree policy is documented but not mechanically enforced. Agents can accidentally run in prohibited root-copy context, which harms reproducibility and increases environment-related failures.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add a validation/pre-commit check that detects and rejects prohibited root-working-copy execution for agent workflows. Provide a clear remediation message pointing to worktree setup steps.

deficiencies.description: Coverage reporting remains summary-only and not machine-consumable in review workflows. Agents and reviewers have weak visibility into where coverage changed, delaying targeted remediation.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Update coverage scripts/workflows to generate `--lcov` and HTML outputs and publish them in CI. Add optional PR reporting so changed-file regressions are visible immediately.

deficiencies.description: Formatting enforcement relies on pre-commit behavior rather than an explicit CI format gate. If hooks are misconfigured or skipped upstream, style drift can merge and create noisy cleanup work for agents.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add `cargo fmt --all --check` to validation scripts and CI workflows as a hard failure. Keep formatting failure output concise so remediation is immediate.

deficiencies.description: Parser coverage is example-driven but lacks property/fuzz validation against arbitrary malformed input. Agents can introduce edge regressions that escape curated examples and only surface during autonomous runtime parsing.
deficiencies.suggested_task_title: Add Property Tests For Parser Invariants
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Introduce `proptest` suites for parser/token helpers with no-panic and invariant expectations across random strings. Add targeted shrink-friendly failure messages for quick debug when invariants break.

deficiencies.description: Fixture intent in migration-wiring script fixtures is implicit and under-documented. Agents updating fixtures may misinterpret expected fail/pass semantics and accidentally codify incorrect behavior.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add a fixture README describing each case, expected output signatures, and extension rules. Keep examples of canonical failure text to stabilize assertions.

deficiencies.description: Pre-commit policy states hooks must pass, but the remediation workflow is not clearly documented. Agents hit failures late, then iterate blindly through fixes without a standardized local pre-flight sequence.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add pre-flight commands and a short fix loop: run hooks, fix issues, re-run targeted checks, then commit. Include common failure categories and where to find canonical scripts.

deficiencies.description: Coverage feedback is primarily log-only in CI without rich artifact publication. Agents and reviewers must parse raw output, which slows regression triage and obscures changed-file coverage impact.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Generate LCOV and HTML outputs from `cargo llvm-cov` and upload them as workflow artifacts. Optionally add PR annotations/comments for changed-file coverage deltas.

deficiencies.description: Architecture pointers for `tools/gardener/src/` are sparse in steering docs. Agents need more time to map responsibilities and are more likely to patch the wrong layer in orchestration workflows.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add a short architecture map in `AGENTS.md` or linked docs naming key modules and ownership boundaries. Include where changes belong for lifecycle, adapters, phases, and CLI entrypoints.

deficiencies.description: Executable docs for orchestration invariants are limited, with key lifecycle rules mostly implicit in code/tests. Agents spend extra turns inferring invariants and may produce incorrect edits in stateful flows.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Create short docs for worker FSM transitions, startup sequencing, and merge-loop decision logic. Link each invariant section to owning tests and representative failure modes.

deficiencies.description: Quick local loop documentation is incomplete for scoped reruns and escalation guidance. Agents often default to heavyweight checks even when a narrow, faster command would provide sufficient confidence.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add a concise section showing file/test-name filtered commands and targeted lint options. Include clear rules for when to escalate from scoped checks to full validation.

deficiencies.description: The broad test suite lacks a local navigation README that maps categories, fixtures, and command selection. Agents spend extra turns selecting and running the wrong scope of tests.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Create `tools/gardener/tests/README.md` documenting suite taxonomy, fixture locations, and change-to-test mapping guidance. Include fast-path commands for common edit types.

deficiencies.description: No unified task runner entrypoint exists for common developer and agent workflows. Command discovery is fragmented across scripts, which increases accidental non-canonical execution paths.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add a thin `justfile` or `Makefile` with targets for hooks, lint, test, coverage, and fast/full validation. Delegate to existing scripts so behavior stays centralized.

deficiencies.description: Shell scripts lack static analysis gates such as `shellcheck` and optional format checks. Agents may introduce quoting/portability defects that fixture tests do not fully detect.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Integrate `shellcheck` (and optionally `shfmt --check`) into `scripts/run-validate.sh` and CI. Fix baseline findings and pin tool behavior for deterministic runs.

deficiencies.description: Telemetry/log behavior appears tested on a limited set of shapes and volumes. Agents relying on logs for diagnosis can misclassify failures when faced with malformed, out-of-order, or high-volume records that were never contract-tested.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add malformed JSONL, out-of-order event, and high-volume truncation cases to OTEL parsing/streaming tests. Verify parse resilience, ordering behavior, and stable failure classification semantics.

deficiencies.description: Many UI assertions depend on substring containment rather than stronger structural invariants. Agents may ship semantic layout regressions that still contain expected text and therefore evade test detection.
deficiencies.suggested_task_details: Add normalized golden/snapshot checks for key layouts across representative terminal sizes. Keep targeted structural assertions for critical sections so tests fail on semantic layout drift, not just missing strings.

primary_gap: The most impactful gap is missing test coverage on runtime boundary modules (`main.rs`, `config.rs`, `phase_cli.rs`, `plan_phase.rs`, `merge_loop.rs`, `pr_audit.rs`), because agents cannot reliably validate orchestration-critical changes before they fail in real runs.

repo_wide_rationale.agent_steering: Steering is clear where it exists: runtime entry commands and key commit/worktree expectations are specific and actionable. The weakness is breadth, not clarity, because guidance does not adequately cover integration-test selection, script workflows, or architecture navigation. This causes autonomous runs to under-validate or spend extra turns discovering commands. The low score reflects narrow coverage of the full engineering workflow.
repo_wide_rationale.coverage_infrastructure: Coverage is genuinely enforced with numeric thresholds and failing CI behavior, which provides a solid baseline. However, summary-only reporting and limited artifact/annotation visibility reduce diagnostic speed for regressions. Exclusions in the ignore manifest also weaken confidence in denominator quality for runtime-critical code. The score reflects strong enforcement with moderate observability and scope trust gaps.
repo_wide_rationale.documentation_quality: Repository-level workflow docs and runbooks are strong, discoverable, and supported by anti-drift checks. This gives contributors and agents a reliable operational baseline. The principal weakness is API-level rustdoc depth and lack of rustdoc/missing-docs enforcement in validation. The score is high overall, but constrained by runtime contract discoverability gaps.
repo_wide_rationale.local_feedback_loop: Local and CI parity is a major strength, with shared scripts producing consistent outcomes across environments. The main problem is iteration latency because commit-time validation is heavy by default and lacks a clearly documented fast tier. Command discoverability is also fragmented without a unified task runner. The score stays good because correctness is high, but throughput can be improved.
repo_wide_rationale.mechanical_guardrails: Guardrails are strong due to CI and pre-commit integration around canonical validation scripts and strict linting/coverage thresholds. This creates reliable hard-fail behavior for many regressions. The score is reduced by missing security/dependency scanning, incomplete format enforcement in CI, and weaker coverage observability outputs. Overall it is robust, but not yet comprehensive.
